about: Every design mock-up, by section, for the gallery at /mockups/ (design/index.html). Add a card here whenever a new mock-up folder lands in design/; `node scripts/mockup-gallery.mjs` refreshes the thumbnails and fails if a folder is missing from this list. Optional `shot`: the address the gallery picture is taken from, when the mock-up's difference is not on its first page.

cards.title: David · Two voices
cards.line: The record and David's psalms in counterpoint, joined by harp strings that vibrate as each moment arrives (only psalms whose title names the moment).

cards.title: David · The house of David
cards.line: Saul's and David's houses as a living tree with a year scrubber: sons appear, branches grey at each death, crowns pass; 1 Kings 1 as a drama.

cards.title: David · War table
cards.line: A tilted 3D table of the land played in 27 turns, from the valley of Elah to Absalom's revolt: pieces rise, arcs fly, no borders invented.

cards.title: David · Life helix
cards.line: A WebGL double helix of his 70 years: Samuel–Kings in gold, Chronicles in silver, rungs where they differ, 46 event crystals; drag to turn.

cards.title: A · The road
cards.line: Recommended. The map is the page: a full-width journey map stays in place while you scroll, the route draws itself act by act, and each scene rises over it as a glass panel.

cards.title: B · Three forties
cards.line: A command-deck hero: a 120-year ring split into the three forties; choose an act and its bento tiles (scenes, people, words, places) fill the screen and open in place.

cards.title: C · Cinema
cards.line: Full-screen chapters, each with a large line drawing (bush, sea, mountain, tent, Nebo); scenes slide sideways within a chapter; the full text waits in drawers.

cards.title: D · Constellation
cards.line: Moses at the centre of a field: rings of people, places, moments and words, clockwise in story order; choose any point and its panel opens beside it, lines drawn to everything it touches.

cards.title: E · Face to face
cards.line: His life told only through the conversations Scripture records: voices as presences (the LORD as light, never a figure), a score of every line, ten places, threads to follow; every word quoted from the KJV.

cards.title: F · In his hands
cards.line: A specimen cabinet of the eleven objects Scripture names in his life, each drawn by hand: open a case for every verse about it, follow each through time, and see the one object Scripture measures to scale.

cards.title: G · The long memory
cards.line: All 786 verses that name him as light across the 66 books: Exodus to Deuteronomy blaze, then the echoes to Revelation; sort by how a verse remembers him or who is speaking, only where the words support it.

cards.title: H · The merged page
cards.line: Newest, second pass. B's three-forties landing as it was; the whole road on one quiet Atlas map with a way into the Atlas; three dense chapters (Egypt, Midian, the wilderness), each with a sky of faint dots, a giant numeral, sideways scenes, every event with its verse, the people, signs, words and world stage in typographic columns, and a line-art landscape for ground; the map slides in beside a chapter and back out; then the man and his family tree, the word, the constellation of the people around him, the questions as floating words, and C's dot navigation down the side.

cards.title: Tribes A · The land
cards.line: A full-screen map: every tribe a constellation of the towns Joshua gives it (Atlas points, no drawn borders), and a history scrubber: allotment, Dan moves north, the kingdom divided, the north carried away, Ezekiel's bands.

cards.title: Tribes B · The camp
cards.line: The tabernacle with the twelve camped round it (Numbers 2), each block a field of dots, one per thousand; toggle Numbers 1 and 26 and watch Simeon shrink; Break camp plays the march of Numbers 10.

cards.title: Tribes C · The family
cards.line: Four mothers as lanes, twelve sons born one by one with the words said at each naming; ribbons cross to the tribes, drawn as wide as the people our data places in each.

cards.title: Tribes D · The ledger
cards.line: Recommended: it draws the brief's own insight. Twenty-five lists as a score, one row per list; Braid turns each tribe into a thread through them; the two blessings as a duet; a fingerprint card per tribe. Keep A's constellation map for the land section.

cards.title: Apostles · The merged page
cards.line: The merged apostle page: a full-screen landing drawn for each of the fourteen (switch at the top right, in the order of Matthew 10, then Matthias and Paul), the record ring, the chapter grid, four cinema chapters in the Moses containers, who was with him (lines or the whole circle), one moment in several accounts each in its own card, his places as cards beside an Atlas-style map that stays on his places, and every open question from the reviewed sources as floating words.

cards.title: Apostles · A · Lifeline
cards.line: Round 3, in the Authors house style (Peter; Paul and Thaddaeus by ?who=). A plain hero with four figures; the life ring in Scripture's four parts; who was with him, every record in story order with each companion as a line that lights where a verse names them together; did their paths cross (Peter and Paul, with the verses); the mission on a NASA Blue Marble globe; questions as floating words.

cards.title: Apostles · B · Chapters
cards.line: The owner's ideal page for an apostle: the life ring as header, a looping line-art scene (the boat and the net; the road and the light; the list of the Twelve), four cinema chapters with giant numerals and faint stars, "See the map" sliding the globe in beside each chapter, the cabinet of things Scripture names, and a second page with everyone on one sky.

cards.title: Apostles · C · Side by side
cards.line: The Preached Bible way: a heat grid of every chapter that names him, one moment told by each Gospel in its own KJV words as quiet columns, crystals by kind of moment, the places as a sideways row of large tiles, the globe for the mission, questions as floating words.

cards.title: E · The score
cards.line: Set aside 2026-10-08: arcade look; the globe kept. Round 2, the apostle page (Peter; Paul and Thaddaeus by ?who=). His life as a score: Matthew, Mark, Luke, John, Acts and the letters are staves, every event a note in the harmony's order; drag the playhead or press play and the scene opens above.

cards.title: F · The globe
cards.line: Set aside 2026-10-08: arcade look; the globe kept. A turning 3D globe of the Roman world: Scripture's journeys as solid arcs, tradition's routes dashed and labelled with who said it and when; scroll and the globe turns to each place, the scene rising beside it.

cards.title: G · The thread
cards.line: Set aside 2026-10-08: arcade look; the globe kept. Every recorded exchange as a message history, word for word from the KJV with its verse: Jesus in red letters, the apostle on the right; Gospel tabs where the wording differs, tradition as forwarded reports, open questions as polls with no votes.

cards.title: H · The strata
cards.line: Set aside 2026-10-08: arcade look; the globe kept. The evidence as the picture: four glass plates stacked in 3D, Scripture at the bottom, then early church, later tradition and scholars, each carrying its claims on one life-line; drag to tilt, explode, and drill a core through every layer.

cards.title: Unseen A · The veil
cards.line: Michael, angels and demons page (/people/:id/unseen). Two realms on one screen: Daniel's three weeks of mourning by the river below, the unseen above as a plain diagram of what Daniel 10 says (who withstood, for how many days, who came to help); scrolling lifts a woven veil between them.

cards.title: Unseen B · War in heaven
cards.line: Michael. Revelation 12 as a night-sky chart in fine line: the woman clothed with the sun, the dragon as a figure of stars with seven crowned heads, Michael and his angels as points of light; each verse lights its part, and on a phone the view follows it.

cards.title: Unseen C · Strata
cards.line: Michael. The evidence as a flat geological section: Scripture as bedrock, then Jewish writings outside the Bible, early church, later tradition and scholars, each layer dated; a drill core goes down and every find opens beside it. Close in idea to the apostle set's glass-plate strata.

cards.title: Unseen D · Who is like God?
cards.line: Recommended. Michael. The name as the centrepiece (מִיכָאֵל in its three parts, with the lexicons' meaning), then the whole Bible as one spine to scale with a light wherever he is named: the planned 'where they appear' picture, and it works for every being in scope. War in heaven's line drawing can serve its visions.

cards.line: Revelation 21's foursquare city with its twelve pearl gates, its wall laid in 1,189 small unnamed stones, one for each chapter in the site's section colours; clicking one sets the centre button to Continue to that chapter. City with sides: Bible, Study and Apologetics down the left and Atlas, Resources and Sources down the right. City with squares: the home page's own doorway squares beside the city instead. City on the word wall: the same in front of mock-up 5's moving wall of Scripture, titled God's Word Stands Forever, its squares edged in gold with Scroll B's hover, a small Hebrew row in place of the marquee, the marquee between the questions and the sources, and mock-up 4's Scroll A with Numbers 6:24-25 and Joshua 1:9 as the last thing before the footer. The row of five doorways under the opening is gone on all three.

cards.title: Home openings A, B, C, D

sections.title: Resources · Help for life

Every national line is collapsed to name, subtitle, one sentence and cost, and opens for every number. Real life.json data, Jacksonville only. Crisis lines keep their call/text buttons on the closed row in all four directions.

cards.line: A column of solid-colour kinds beside a dense list; every line, crisis or not, has its first call or text button on the right of its closed row.

cards.title: Hero drawing · twenty-four to choose from
cards.line: Twenty-four slowly looping line drawings for the top of the page, in three grids of eight, each with its King James verse: still waters, the shepherd of Isaiah 40, a lamp, wings over a nest, an open door, a lighthouse on the rock, morning, a mended plant, then a boat on a calm sea, a well, loaves and fishes, an anchor, a vine, a valley path, the dove with the olive leaf, an eagle, then a mustard tree with birds, a tent under the stars, a rainbow, sheaves, lilies of the field, a tree by the river, a window in the rain and a city on a hill. Say the number to choose.

sections.title: Study · New theology studies
sections.line: New Scripture & Theology studies, built from the written drafts.

cards.title: Faith in daily life
cards.line: Six everyday places in the letters, read in the Berean under the Baptist Faith and Message. Its new move: ask the sentence why, each instruction's own reason sorted toward the Lord or toward another person.

cards.title: Faith under pressure
cards.line: Six pressures in the letters, read in the Berean under the Baptist Faith and Message. Its new move: name the pressure, find the ground, every verse laid out with what it names, what it calls for and what it stands on.

cards.title: Faith under pressure: the wall
cards.line: A dry-stone wall where every stone is a verse, as long as the verse is. Six piers take six different loads: arrows of many kinds, a door in the wall, a load cast off, words thrown from one side, one stone missing with a small light in its place, a prop of other people's help.

cards.title: Covenants and promises
cards.line: Five covenants and how the letters read them, in the Berean under the Baptist Faith and Message. Its new move: ask every promise the same five questions, then see the whole Bible as one line with arcs to the verses that come back to it.

cards.title: Covenants and promises: the signs
cards.line: The same study, wholly different. Each covenant is a full-width world and its sign holds the five questions: a bow, stars, stone, a crown, a cup. The later verses ripple across a disc of the whole Bible, and the signs move into each map.

cards.title: The good news
cards.line: For someone who is not a Christian, or is not sure. Read the gospel as news before advice: seven verses with what God has done on the left and what it calls for on the right, then six parts down one thread like a road home, Luke 15's three lost things as fields of dots, and six honest questions.

cards.title: The hope to come
cards.line: Christ's return, the resurrection, the judgment and the new creation, in the Berean under the Baptist Faith and Message. Its new move: three questions for any passage about the end, then four orders of events lined up on the return, without choosing.

cards.title: The hope to come: the horizon
cards.line: The same study, wholly different. One land seen from one place: sky is what is promised, haze what it leaves open, ground what it asks now. Six readings, one at a time, each with its own drawn view; what was lost and answered on facing pages from dusk to dawn; four orders of events on one chart, lined up on the return.

cards.title: The shape of Scripture
cards.line: The page changes its shape with the writing: a command cut in stone, a psalm that climbs, the last page of Luke facing the first of Acts, a letter set as a letter. Then one kind of writing across the books, a staircase of later parts looking back, and three passages to name yourself.

cards.title: Humanity, sin and renewal
cards.line: One line and one body. Six passages on a line whose height is named and is not worth, each opening with its words and three questions in its margin; the same body as Paul lists it in Romans 3 and as Romans 6:13 hands it over; Romans 5 as two sides and a hinge; and the word image followed through Scripture.

cards.title: Prophets in their times
cards.line: The opening verses, taken at their word. Rulers in rows with no years, and a prophet touches only the rulers the text names; six books name no ruler and are left unplaced. Each opening verse set large with what it names and what it does not; six questions asked of any prophet; and a record of 108 lines where an empty line stays empty.

cards.title: Witness and the nations
cards.line: Reshaped for the new study. In any passage about witness, ask whose part is whose: what God does, what is given to the one who speaks, what belongs to the one who hears. Romans 10:14-15's chain of five links, read backward as Paul reads it; seven passages, each with its limits; all seven set against the three questions in one table; questions readers ask; and a close on Romans 10:9-17.

cards.title: A new creation
cards.line: Reshaped for the rewritten text. One fold down the page: what a letter says is already so on the left, what it tells you to do on the right, the letter's own joining word on the crease. Six parts each open beneath their line; the six places the text names; the close's five "so"s across the same fold; and six hard questions.

cards.title: Prayer across Scripture
cards.line: Reshaped around the Lord's Prayer for the rewritten text. Don't stop at the request; ask, so that what? The prayer Jesus taught set as ruled lines, each line opening a part; each letter passage kept whole on a leaf, broken into lines that step in at each so that; six letter prayers read from the bottom up, from thanks to where each arrives; and six questions, faced.

cards.title: The church and its calling
cards.line: Who was in the room? One word in four sizes: every use of church or churches in the Berean New Testament as a point on four rings, from a house to all who are Christ's; six readings behind six small drawings, each opening with who was listening; ten baptisms down one line of water; six phrases of 1 Peter beside older verses; three lines tried in their rooms; and six hard questions.

cards.title: Rulers and their choices
cards.line: How does a verdict get written? Two beams, one for each kingdom: all 39 rulers in Kings on a string as long as the reign the text states, ending in the writer's verdict, with threads back to the two names that come back most; six readings, each in a form its own text gives; six kings told by Kings and by Chronicles, parting and joining; three royal letters, one row for each hand, ending in Esther; and six hard questions.

cards.title: Encounters with Jesus
cards.line: Who moved first, and where does the record stop? Fifteen meetings on one plate, each with its drawing and last line in words; what you are carrying lights the meetings that held it; seven groups, each in a form its own passage gives; only the six Scripture sees again run on; nine things often said, tested against the text; and five hard questions.

cards.title: The signs and works of Jesus
cards.line: Where does the deed fall, and how much stands around it? Eight accounts as cords on a warm-brown band, one touching length for each of 179 verses, a star on the 16 that tell the deed, with a lens for each kind of verse and three unmarked accounts to try; six readings, each in a form its own text gives; the same deed and not the same response, in the accounts' own words; Scripture in three voices; and five hard questions.

cards.title: Who do you say that I am?
cards.line: Reshaped for the rewritten text. For someone who does not yet believe: keep the words attached to the person who said them. 47 things people said about Jesus, each in the speaker's own Berean words, as type on fine rules, with a ruled blank to try them in; eight words that light who else used them; six scenes each in a form from its own passage; a new ledger of who says the Word became flesh, and to whom; five hard questions; and a blank left for the reader that keeps nothing.

cards.title: Saved by grace
cards.line: Watch who is doing the verbs. Six passages as six columns of a verb chart, people acting before the word "But" and God after it, with James, which has no such turn; a switch marks every verb in the printed Scripture; Luke 18's two prayers, Romans 4's four bookkeeping words and Abraham's two moments on one line.

cards.title: The cross, the empty tomb and the throne
cards.line: Every picture of the cross has a home. Paul's four lines (died, buried, raised, appeared) and the throne as five steps up the page; six pictures (temple, slave market, friendship, law court, battlefield, family) round one centre, each showing where it stops; then at the empty tomb, not a picture but a report: who saw what.

cards.title: The book of Psalms
cards.line: Before you read a psalm, find where it stands in the book. All 150 psalms in one picture (the gate, five books, four closing blessings, the ending of praise), seen four ways, and every part of the study points back into it.

cards.title: Genesis 1-11: the questions readers bring
cards.line: Read the verse before the view. The eleven chapters as one band, each as wide as its verses, narrowing to Genesis 12:1; eight questions as arcs over the verses they read, each in three tiers: what the text says, the readings side by side with none lit, and where the text stops.

cards.title: Angels, demons and spiritual powers
cards.line: Read the text as far as it goes, and stop where it stops. Deuteronomy 29:29 drawn as a line: an edge chart of what each part's text reveals and what it leaves unsaid, then every part in full light up to a dashed rule marked "Here the text stops", with the views beyond it shown, not chosen.

cards.title: Christ in the Old Testament
cards.line: Draw only the lines the New Testament draws, then look for where each picture stops. The Law, the Prophets and the Psalms (Luke 24:44), with lines from five figures to the New Testament verses that draw them, each line ending where the shadow ends (Colossians 2:17).

cards.title: Sexuality, singleness and divorce
cards.line: Find the question a hard verse was answering, then go back to the beginning. Matthew 19:3-12 drawn first as seven turns of one conversation over a ground line marked "From the beginning"; every part then carries one rule with three stations: From the beginning, Asked first, Holiness and grace.

cards.title: What Scripture promises the sick
cards.line: Ask what kind of word a verse is, when it is kept, and who is speaking. A register of the ten sick people the study reads, from Publius's father to Trophimus, in the verses' own words: four recover, six are left ill, kept in weakness or not told; one line runs under all of them (Romans 8:23; Revelation 21:4).

cards.title: Women of the Bible
cards.line: Read her story first, then how later Scripture remembers her. One chart of sixteen stories with a curve from each to every later book that looks back on her; then the stories themselves, facing each other in the pairs and trios the text sets them in.

cards.title: Leviticus: holiness and sacrifice
cards.line: Read each law twice, where it stood in Israel and what the New Testament does with it, then ask what it asks of you. One plan of the camp read two ways; Israel and the New Testament side by side in every part, with where the reading stops beneath.

cards.title: Reading Daniel and Revelation
cards.line: Read a vision from the throne outward. Daniel told to seal his book and John told not to; the two books' opposite orders of beasts and throne side by side; both drawn chapter by chapter with every verse that names a throne or a beast; seven parts down a scroll whose seals break as each is read.

cards.title: Life together
cards.line: Look under the command. Every "one another" command stands above a ground line, with a root running down to the gift it rests on, as deep as the gift is far from the command in the text, measured by script; eight passages in six parts, from John 13 to Romans 15.

cards.title: Learning to discern
cards.line: Put three questions to a claim, in order: what it says about Jesus, whether it is so in the passage read whole, and what is driving me as I judge it. A claim's line through three stations, the third bending back to the reader; a rail beside every part shows which question it trains.

cards.title: The kingdom he announced
cards.line: Listen for the tense. Jesus' kingdom sayings set out as a grammar book sets out a verb (is near, has come upon you, is in your midst, will be like), one line for each part, and each part carries its line.

cards.title: Following Jesus
cards.line: Read the line inside the whole. The Sermon on the Mount as one band of 111 verse marks under Matthew's two frames; ten famous lines placed at their verses with who was listening and what came before; the band follows the six parts, each with one drawing from its own verses.

cards.title: God: who He is and what He does
cards.line: When a passage tells you what God is like, look in it for what He is doing. Seven words on one dotted orbit, each tied by a fine line to its deed; ten passages read one at a time under Name, Character, Creation and Providence; every verse of the Berean that calls God slow to anger.

cards.title: The Holy Spirit
cards.line: When a passage speaks of the Spirit, ask where He is pointing. A floodlight whose lamp is never shown: six beams, one for each reading, falling on three places (Jesus, new life, other people), two on each (John 16:14).

cards.title: What the Bible says about itself
cards.line: When a verse is quoted, read around it and ask what it is being used to do. Matthew 4's four "it is written" lines, three spoken by Jesus and one by the devil, each traced back to the verses it was taken from; then the six claims the Bible makes about itself.

cards.title: Reading the Bible well
cards.line: Read a verse inside the book it belongs to. A lamp on a path of stepping stones lights only the next three (Psalm 119:105); Jonah read from the whole book inward, one line down to the roots of the mountains and back; Jeremiah 29:11 read outward, from a card to its place in the letter.

cards.title: The story of the Bible
cards.line: Before you read any verse, ask where you are in the story. A map with a you-are-here pin: eight stations on one road from the garden to the city, six promise threads beneath; choosing a station answers where am I, what has God promised by now, and what is still waiting.

cards.title: Fear, anxiety and despair
cards.line: When a passage records someone's darkest words, keep reading to what God does next. The distance in verses: two for Moses, one for Elijah, 870 for Job; Psalm 56:3 holds fear and trust in one sentence; Psalm 88 runs to its end with no turn. Help comes first, before the lead.

cards.title: Grief and dying
cards.line: Before you ask what a grief passage explains, ask who is weeping, and to whom. Every mourner joined by one fine line to the one their words go to; then the days of mourning, the Song of the Bow, all 154 verses of Lamentations with the hope at its middle, and the comma in Luke 23:43.

cards.title: Chosen and kept
cards.line: Before you ask whether a verse is about you, ask what it was written to do. Eight passages sorted by purpose (to praise, to comfort, to warn, to answer) before any is read; each part marked with its purpose and ending on the close's own sentence for it.

cards.title: Baptism and the Lord's Supper
cards.line: Ask what the sign points to, and what came before it. "Water once. Bread again and again." drawn as one line of a believer's life that goes under the water once and passes the table again and again toward "until He comes"; seven parts read with the same two questions.

cards.title: Children and the home
cards.line: Before you hold a verse as a promise, ask what kind of sentence it is. Every quotation carries its kind in the margin (command, song, story or saying) with what that kind asks of you; choosing a kind marks it down the page; each part ends with what its passage does not promise.

cards.title: The Ten Commandments
cards.line: Rescue first, then the words. The counting table with three ways of counting; the opening sentence as a lintel over two arched stones; where Exodus 20 and Deuteronomy 5 differ; which words three New Testament passages take up; and the week, first day and seventh.

cards.title: Every life in God's image
cards.line: When a passage tells you how to treat a person, look around the scene for the one who cannot speak. Each passage drawn as a room seen from above (the womb, the king's table, the church meeting, the court at the gate, the bedside), and the close names the five the rooms find.

cards.title: Money, possessions and generosity
cards.line: Before you claim a promise about money, read the address on it. Every passage carries a postmark and address lines on dotted rules; five often-lifted lines shown first as they are heard, then one switch puts their addresses back; seven parts, each with a figure from its own passage.

cards.title: The Christian and the state
cards.line: Sort what a passage gives the ruler and what it keeps for God alone, then ask whether the two are at peace or in collision. Mark 12:17 as two columns at once, God's larger because Caesar is inside it; six parts, each with its two columns; three questions readers bring, side by side.

cards.title: The wisdom books
cards.line: Before you ask what a line promises, ask who is speaking and what kind of saying it is. Every printed passage carries a speaker line; four books as four columns; Job 28's shaft, what God asks Job, the two doors of Proverbs 1-9, a mirrored pair, Ecclesiastes' fourteen pairs and the Song's refrain.

sections.title: Study · The standard
sections.line: What the studies rated best are made of, for building new ones.

cards.title: Study visual inventory
cards.line: Every visual tool on the eleven studies the standard rates best, cut from the pages in light and dark: what each holds, how a reader uses it, when it fits.

sections.title: Games · Odd one out deck
sections.line: A stack of the odd ones cards on the screen while a round is played, in the game only.

cards.title: Odd one out · the stack during play
cards.line: Each answer drops that puzzle's odd one onto a stack beside the puzzle (a hand of cards above the question on a phone): one sentence, the book that names it most, its era, map point or place among the books, and why it was odd. The start screen is unchanged.
